items.title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
items.description: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have announced a "return hub" for failed asylum seekers.

items.title: Houthi rebel advance in Yemen may further destabilise global economy
items.description: The Iran-backed Houthis are gaining ground and their advance could have dangerous consequences, writes the BBC's security correspondent.

items.title: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex CEO
items.description: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.

items.title: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war
items.description: Russia said Ukraine had launched over 2,000 drones over the course of a day, while Kyiv came under a record 17 air raid alerts.

items.title: When will we see Robert Pattinson as Bond in cinemas?
items.description: Robert Pattinson has been announced as the next James Bond, becoming the seventh actor to take up the mantle of 007.

items.title: Forensic expert says his analysis of autopsy photos suggests Epstein was killed
items.description: Professor Michael Freeman tells BBC Newsnight that he believes the convicted sex offender's injuries are consistent with a homicide.

items.title: Lindsay Clancy to face retrial next year for deaths of her three children
items.description: The 36-year-old's first trial this year fell apart when a 12-person jury failed to reach a verdict.

items.title: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 17 dead
items.description: The shootings in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng highlight South Africa's struggle to curb violent crime.

items.title: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction
items.description: The French film star was due to start an appeal trial after being found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a Paris set.

items.title: Raye, Rosalía and Dolly Parton recognised in Grammy nominations
items.description: British singer Raye lands 11 nominations while Dolly Parton is recognised two months after her death.

items.title: Ashes of exiled Nobel Laureate Miguel Ángel Asturias returned to Guatemala
items.description: The poet, writer and diplomat died in Europe in 1974 having been forced to leave his native country.

items.title: Estonia to close Russia border crossings after attempted drone factory arson attack
items.description: The Estonian government says Russia was behind the attempted sabotage, which the Kremlin denies.
